statement: Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r, r equals the number of ordered index triples (i, j, k) such that 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= k < len(c), and the integer a[i] XOR b[j] XOR c[k] has an even number of set bits, i.e. the number of 1s in its binary representation is even.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, triplet_count(a, b, c) returns some result r; it does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, panic, or any other failure.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r, 0 <= r.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r, r <= len(a) * len(b) * len(c).
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r, r = len(a) * len(b) * len(c) if and only if for every index triple (i, j, k) with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= k < len(c), the integer a[i] XOR b[j] XOR c[k] has an even number of set bits.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there is no ordered index triple (i, j, k) with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= k < len(c) such that a[i] XOR b[j] XOR c[k] has an even number of set bits. Equivalently, r > 0 if and only if at least one such even-parity triple exists.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r and triplet_count(a', b', c') returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100. Let a', b', c' be slices with len(a') = len(a), len(b') = len(b), len(c') = len(c), every entry in 0..100, and each of a', b', c' is a permutation of the corresponding original list: there exist bijections pi_a, pi_b, pi_c on the index sets such that a'[i] = a[pi_a(i)] for all 0 <= i < len(a), b'[j] = b[pi_b(j)] for all 0 <= j < len(b), and c'[k] = c[pi_c(k)] for all 0 <= k < len(c).

statement: For any permutation (x, y, z) of the three lists (a, b, c), i.e. any of the six orders, whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r and triplet_count(x, y, z) returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100.

statement: Define E_a to be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(a) for which the number of set bits of a[i] is even, and O_a = len(a) - E_a. Define E_b, O_b, E_c, O_c analogously. Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r, r = E_a * E_b * E_c + E_a * O_b * O_c + O_a * E_b * O_c + O_a * O_b * E_c.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r and triplet_count(a', b, c) returns a result r', we have r' = r + m.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) < 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100. Additionally x is an integer with 0 <= x <= 100. Let a' be the slice obtained by appending x to a: len(a') = len(a) + 1, a'[i] = a[i] for 0 <= i < len(a), and a'[len(a)] = x. Let m be the number of pairs (j, k) with 0 <= j < len(b) and 0 <= k < len(c) such that x XOR b[j] XOR c[k] has an even number of set bits.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c1) returns a result r1, triplet_count(a, b, c2) returns a result r2, and triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r, we have r = r1 + r2.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100. Let c1 and c2 be nonempty slices such that c = c1 ++ c2 (concatenation); in particular len(c1) >= 1, len(c2) >= 1, len(c1) + len(c2) = len(c), and all entries of c1 and c2 are between 0 and 100.

statement: Whenever triplet_count(a, b, c) returns a result r, r = the sum over i from 0 to len(a)-1 of m_i, where for each i, m_i is the number of pairs (j, k) with 0 <= j < len(b) and 0 <= k < len(c) such that a[i] XOR b[j] XOR c[k] has an even number of set bits.
preconditions: a, b, and c are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(a) <= 100, 1 <= len(b) <= 100, 1 <= len(c) <= 100, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(a), 0 <= a[i] <= 100; for every index j with 0 <= j < len(b), 0 <= b[j] <= 100; for every index k with 0 <= k < len(c), 0 <= c[k] <= 100.
